obernants.approximation_semantics: Conditional source relation; candidate inner complement bound or ambiguous converse
obernants.assumptions: Domain: finite valid byte files, bounded IDs and successful allocation; an operation's arguments plus its initial filesystem and scheduler state are inputs. Observations include returns/errors and written bytes. No simultaneous writer, path traversal, malformed offsets or crash is assumed unless explicitly modeled. Source-derived conditional relation, not a proof of all Rust executions. Evidence: tests.md distinguishes executed probes from proposed oracles.

obernants.operator: U is well-formed finite store/query x ID vectors. U minus R includes a pure conjunction introducing an ID absent from initial 0..len and unknown-feature>=1 accepting any candidate. Candidate inner bound; all absent postings count zero. Probe exercises both >=1 and =0.

obernants.operator: Given selected S for feature>=c, compatible postings assign each surviving candidate at least c and excluded candidates below c, with unconstrained rows outside candidates. For c=0 all candidates survive and no positive-count information is recoverable. Probe finite count threshold fibers.

obernants.operator: Stable or exact-model stamps return parsed IDs without reselecting. order: stamps additionally compare daily key and base. Stale sampled/prefix stamps recompute and overwrite before ancestry discovery. Eligible pointwise ancestor stamps use union changed IDs; unrelated stamps recompute. Missing query defaults empty; malformed ID lines are ignored. Probe stable, same-model, ancestor and unrelated paths plus repaired sampled regression. Pointwise carry still requires membership stability outside changed IDs.

obernants.operator: For fixed seed and ordered candidates, xorshift keys depend on position and IDs; sorted(key,id), take(k), then sort(ids) defines output. k>=len returns all IDs sorted. Swapping sample/filter can change size and membership. Probe searches a two-book fixture for a seed witnessing noncommutation.
